extracted.intended_audience: FCC officials implementing debt collection, creditor agencies, employers, and employees/debtors subject to Commission debt-collection procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for the Commission's collection of debts owed to the United States, including salary offset from employees, administrative wage garnishment, notifications, hearings, interest/penalty assessment, refunds, and interagency responsibilities under 5 U.S.C. 5514 and related authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to private collection contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may refer debts to private collection contractors pursuant to a contract between the Commission and the private collection contractor in those situations where the Commission is not required to transfer debt to the Secretary of the Treasury for debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may fund private collection contractors in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3718(d) or as otherwise permitted by law. Contracts for locating and recovering U.S. assets must have procedures acceptable to Treasury before entering into contracts to recover assets held by state governments or financial institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts for debtor asset and income search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may enter into contracts for debtor asset and income search reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3718(d), such contracts may provide that the fee a contractor charges the Commission for such services may be payable from the amounts recovered; fees will be added to the amount collected and are part of the administrative collection costs passed on to the debtor. See § 1.1940.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary offset purpose and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1.1925 through 1.1939 apply to Commission employees and provide standards to implement 5 U.S.C. 5514 to recover a debt from the pay account of a Commission employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions govern collection by offset from current pay (administrative offset) and should be consistent with the Federal Claims Collection Standards (31 CFR parts 900-904) where not specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded debts from salary offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures in this section do not apply to debts arising under the Internal Revenue Code, the Social Security Act, the tariff laws, or where collection by salary offset is explicitly provided for or prohibited by another statute (examples: travel advances 5 U.S.C. 5705; employee training expenses 5 U.S.C. 4108).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1.1926 does not preclude employees from requesting waiver of erroneous payments under appropriate statutory waiver authorities (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 5584).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to initiate offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 31 CFR 901.3(a)(4) offset may not be initiated more than 10 years after the Government's right to collect the debt first accrued, unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to section 901.3(a)(4) for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary offset notification content
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 30 days before any deduction the Managing Director (or designee) must provide written notice to the employee stating at a minimum items (1) through (13): Commission's determination the debt is owed (origin, nature, amount); intent to collect by deduction from current disposable pay; frequency and amount of intended deduction (fixed dollar or percentage not to exceed 15% of disposable pay) and intent to continue until paid; explanation of policy on interest/penalties/administrative costs; right to inspect and copy government records related to the debt; opportunity to establish voluntary repayment schedule or written agreement; right to a hearing; method/time period for petitioning; filing for hearing stays collection; hearing decision timing (not later than 60 days unless delay requested); warning about false/misleading/frivolous statements and potential disciplinary/criminal penalties; other rights/remedies; statement that amounts paid/deducted later waived or found not owed will be promptly refunded unless contrary statutory/contractual provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications shall be hand delivered with a record of delivery date or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested. See exceptions in paragraph (c) for minor or routine adjustments where full notice/hearing not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification delivery method and limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications under the section must be hand delivered with a date record or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification/hearing/written responses or final decisions are required for: (1) adjustments from employee benefit elections accumulated over four pay periods or less; (2) routine intra-Commission pay adjustments to correct overpayments attributable to clerical/administrative errors if overpayment occurred within prior four pay periods (or as soon thereafter as practical) and written notice is provided; (3) adjustments to collect $50 or less if written notice and point of contact are provided at or soon after adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for hearing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee may request a hearing by filing a written petition with the Managing Director stating why the employee believes the Commission's determination is in error; petition must be executed under penalty of perjury and fully identify and explain with reasonable specificity all facts, evidence, and witnesses supporting the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be filed no later than 15 calendar days from hand delivery or certified mail delivery; late petitions may be accepted upon written showing of circumstances beyond control or failure to receive notice. Failure to file within the time limit (absent acceptance of late filing) waives right to hearing and salary offset will be implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing form, procedures and decision content
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing official will determine the form and content of the hearing, considering nature and complexity of the transaction; hearing may be informal or formal; employee may be self-represented or represented by counsel; hearing official shall maintain a summary record and issue a written decision that states facts, analysis, findings, conclusions, and, if applicable, repayment schedule. The decision shall constitute the final administrative decision of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing official must be outside the control of the Commission (administrative law judge or other lawful arrangement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction limits and installment rules for salary offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily debts will be collected in full in one lump sum if funds available; if the employee cannot pay lump sum or debt exceeds 15% of disposable pay for a pay interval, collection must be in installments. Installment size will bear a reasonable relationship to debt size and employee ability to pay; installments will not exceed 15% of disposable pay unless employee agrees in writing to a greater amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deductions will generally commence with the next full pay interval following employee's consent, waiver of hearing, or hearing decision. Installments will be pro-rated for a period not greater than the anticipated period of employment except as provided in § 1.1930.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation from final check and recovery from other payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the employee leaves employment before collection completes, the Commission may offset the remaining balance from any final payment (e.g., final salary, lump-sum leave) to liquidate the debt; if not liquidated by final payment, offset may be made from later payments due from the United States including Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund pursuant to § 1.1913.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creditor agency must submit properly certified claim to agency responsible for such payments before collection can be made from those sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-waiver of rights by involuntary payments
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee's involuntary payment of all or any portion of a debt collected under 5 U.S.C. 5514 shall not be construed as a waiver of any rights the employee may have under 5 U.S.C. 5514 or other law or contract unless statutory or contractual provisions provide otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for waived or incorrectly owed debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds shall promptly be made when a debt is waived or otherwise found not owing to the United States, or when an employee's paying agency is directed by administrative or judicial order to refund amounts deducted from current pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds do not bear interest unless required or permitted by law or contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor agency certification and submission responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of procedures under 5 U.S.C. 5514 the creditor agency must certify in writing that employee owes the debt, amount and basis, date payments are due, date Government's right to collect first accrued, and that the creditor agency's implementing regulations were approved by OPM; advise Commission if collection in installments (number/amount/commencement date); advise Commission of actions taken under 5 U.S.C. 5514(b) and dates; submit a debt claim with specified information and an installment agreement if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employee is separating, creditor agency must submit claim to Commission for collection pursuant to § 1.1930; if employee already separated, creditor agency may request administrative offset from other Federal payments (e.g., Civil Service Retirement) unless prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission responsibilities on receiving creditor agency claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When Commission receives a properly certified debt claim, deductions should be scheduled to begin prospectively at the next official pay interval and the Commission will notify the employee that a certified debt claim was received (including amount) and provide written notice of the date deductions will commence and amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim is incomplete, Commission will return claim with notice that procedures under 5 U.S.C. 5514 and the subpart must be provided and a properly certified claim received before action can be taken. The Commission will not review the merits of the creditor agency's determination with respect to amount or validity of the certified debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining services of a hearing official (interagency arrangements)
rubrics_metrics.description: When debtor does not work for creditor agency and creditor agency cannot provide a prompt/appropriate hearing, creditor agency may contact an agent of the Commission designated in Appendix A of 5 CFR part 581 for a hearing official and the Commission will cooperate as provided by the FCCS; similar interagency arrangements apply when debtor works for creditor agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of a hearing official designated under this section is considered an official certification regarding existence and amount of the debt for purposes of executing salary offset. If hearing official determines debt may not be collected by salary offset but creditor agency still believes debt valid, creditor agency may pursue other collection remedies (offset of other Federal payments, litigation, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of administrative wage garnishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative wage garnishment procedures apply to Commission-administered programs that give rise to delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States and to the Commission's pursuit of recovery of such debt; these procedures apply notwithstanding any provision of State law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section does not apply to collection of delinquent nontax debt from Federal employees' wages from their Federal employment, which are subject to Federal salary offset procedures (5 U.S.C. 5514, §§ 1.1925-1.1935). Receipt of payments under garnishment does not preclude other remedies; garnishment may be combined with other remedies. Nothing requires duplication of notices/proceedings required by contract or other laws/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions applicable to wage garnishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Key defined terms include business day (Mon-Fri; last day included unless Federal holiday), day (calendar day; last day included unless Sat/Sun/Federal holiday), certificate of service (signed by Commission official indicating nature/date/recipient of mailed document), disposable pay (compensation remaining after deduction of health insurance and amounts required by law to be withheld), amounts required by law to be withheld (e.g., social security and withholding taxes, not court-ordered withholdings), employer (entity that pays wages; includes state/local governments but not Federal agencies), garnishment (withholding from disposable pay to pay creditor), withholding order (order for withholding or garnishment by agency/judicial/administrative body).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are used to interpret garnishment procedures and compute time periods and withholding amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule for initiating wage garnishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Commission determines that a delinquent debt is owed by an individual, the Commission may initiate proceedings administratively to garnish the wages of the delinquent debtor as governed by procedures prescribed by 31 CFR 285.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage garnishment will usually be performed for the Commission by the Treasury as part of debt collection for Commission debts referred to Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements prior to initiating garnishment
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 30 days before initiation of garnishment proceedings the Commission shall mail by first class mail to the debtor's last known address a written notice informing the debtor of: (i) the nature and amount of the debt; (ii) the intention to initiate deductions from pay until debt and accumulated interest/penalties/admin costs are paid in full; and (iii) an explanation of the debtor's rights and the time frame to exercise them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debtor must be afforded opportunity to inspect/copy records, enter into a written repayment agreement under acceptable terms, and request a hearing concerning existence/amount of debt or terms of proposed repayment schedule (except no hearing entitlement for terms already established by written agreement). The Commission will keep a certificate of service indicating mailing date; certificate may be retained electronically if evidentiary standards met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedures for wage garnishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts by reference the hearing procedures of 31 CFR 285.11(f), affording the debtor the hearing rights specified therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 31 CFR 285.11(f) for detailed hearing procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content of wage garnishment withholding order
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless Commission receives information justifying delay/cancellation, the Commission will send a withholding order to the debtor's employer within 30 days after the debtor fails to make a timely request for a hearing (i.e., within 15 business days after mailing the notice) or within 30 days after a final decision to proceed with garnishment, or as soon as reasonably possible thereafter. The order shall be in a form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury on Commission letterhead, signed by head of Commission or delegate, and contain only necessary information for employer compliance, including debtor name, address, SSN, withholding instructions, and where payments should be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will keep a certificate of service of mailing; certificate may be retained electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer certification responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with the withholding order the Commission shall send an employer certification form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury; the employer must complete and return the certification within the timeframe in the form instructions addressing debtor employment status and disposable pay available for withholding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer must respond in the timeframe to facilitate proper withholding calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts withheld under garnishment and priority rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a garnishment order the employer shall deduct from disposable pay the amount of garnishment. The amount withheld shall be the lesser of: (i) amount indicated on the garnishment order up to 15% of the debtor's disposable pay; or (ii) the amount set forth in 15 U.S.C. 1673(a)(2) (amount by which disposable pay exceeds an amount equivalent to thirty times the minimum wage). When pay is subject to withholding orders with priority, orders under this section have priority over later-served withholding orders, but family support withholding orders have priority over these orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amounts are being withheld under prior orders, the amount under this section shall be the lesser of the normal calculation or an amount equal to 25% of disposable pay less amounts already withheld under prior orders. The Commission may issue multiple withholding orders for multiple debts owed to the Commission provided total garnished does not exceed the amount in paragraph (i)(2). An amount greater than set forth may be withheld upon written consent of debtor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer remittance and pay cycle limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer shall promptly pay to the Commission all amounts withheld and shall not be required to vary its normal pay and disbursement cycles to comply with the withholding order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must withhold the appropriate amount each pay period until notified by Commission to discontinue; withholding order shall indicate reasonable period within which employer must commence withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from garnishment for involuntary separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not garnish wages of a debtor it knows has been involuntarily separated from employment until the debtor has been reemployed continuously for at least 12 months. The debtor has burden of informing the Commission of involuntary separation circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial hardship review and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A debtor subject to a withholding order may request a Commission review of the amount garnished based on materially changed circumstances (disability, divorce, catastrophic illness) resulting in demonstrated financial hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debtor must submit basis for claiming financial hardship with supporting documentation. Demonstrated financial hardship must be based on financial records including Federal and state tax returns, affidavits under penalty of perjury, and for business-related hardships, full financial statements (audited or under oath) per Commission procedures/standards. If hardship found, Commission may downwardly adjust garnished amount for an agreeable period and notify employer of adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending garnishment and account review
rubrics_metrics.description: Once Commission has fully recovered amounts owed (including interest, penalties, administrative costs consistent with FCCS), Commission will notify employer to discontinue withholding. At least annually the Commission shall review debtor accounts to ensure garnishment has been terminated for paid-in-full accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer prohibited actions regarding withholding orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer may not discharge, refuse to employ, or take disciplinary action against a debtor due to issuance of a withholding order under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds when garnishment determined improper
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hearing official determines that a debt is not legally due and owing, the Commission shall promptly refund any amount collected by means of administrative wage garnishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless required by law or contract, such refunds shall not bear interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission right of action against noncomplying employer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may sue any employer for any amount the employer fails to withhold from wages in accordance with withholding order paragraphs. A suit may not be filed before termination of the collection action involving the particular debtor unless earlier filing is necessary to avoid statute of limitation expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination of collection action is when Commission has terminated collection action in accordance with FCCS or not received any payments to satisfy debt for a period of one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of interest, penalties, and administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, the Commission shall charge interest, penalties, and administrative costs on debts pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3717. Written notice to debtor at CORES contact address must explain Commission's requirements concerning these charges unless included in contract/repayment agreement or otherwise provided in rules. Charges continue to accrue until debt paid or resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These charges do not modify contract terms or other rights unless provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest rate rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest shall accrue from date of delinquency (or as provided by contract/note/regulation). Unless otherwise established, interest rate charged shall be the rate established annually by the Treasury in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3717. An agency may charge a higher rate if it reasonably determines necessary to protect U.S. rights and documents reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial rate remains fixed for duration of indebtedness. When debtor defaults on repayment agreement and enters new agreement, agency may require interest at a new rate reflecting current Treasury value at time of new agreement execution. Interest shall not be compounded (no interest on interest, penalties, or administrative costs). Charges accrued but not collected under a defaulted agreement may be added to principal under a new agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and calculation of administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall assess administrative costs incurred for processing and handling delinquent debts unless prohibited by statute. Calculation may be based on actual costs or estimated costs as determined by Commission. Administrative costs include personnel and service costs (e.g., telephone, copier, overhead) to notify and collect the debt, regardless of collection success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty rate for delinquent debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise established, Commission will charge a penalty pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3717(e)(2), currently not to exceed six percent (6%) a year on amount due on a debt delinquent for more than 90 days. This charge shall accrue from date of delinquency. If the statutory permitted rate changes, Commission will apply that rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-of-living adjustment alternative for administrative debt
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may increase an administrative debt by the cost-of-living adjustment in lieu of charging interest and penalties. Administrative debt includes debts based on fines, penalties, and overpayments but not debts based on extension of Government credit (loans/guaranties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COLA is percentage by which Consumer Price Index for June of preceding calendar year exceeds CPI for June of year debt was determined/last adjusted. Increases computed annually and used only when legitimate reason exists, e.g., when calculating interest/penalties is extremely difficult due to debt age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application order for partial or installment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a debt is paid in partial or installment payments, amounts received shall be applied first to outstanding penalties and administrative cost charges, second to accrued interest, and third to outstanding principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of interest and administrative charges for prompt payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will waive collection of interest and administrative charges on the portion of the debt that is paid within 30 days after the date on which interest began to accrue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will not extend the 30-day period except for good cause shown of extraordinary and compelling circumstances, fully documented and submitted before the expiration of the first 30-day period.
